name: Beijing Daxing International Airport
before:
Beijing's second international airport, and the one that decides which alliance your client flies. SkyTeam carriers and some Oneworld members work from here, while Hainan Airlines and most of Star Alliance stayed at Beijing Capital, 65 km to the north. Check the alliance before booking a connection, because the two airports are nowhere near each other.

It opened in September 2019 and is hard to mistake for anywhere else. The terminal is a single building of 700,000 square metres, the largest of its kind anywhere, laid out in the starfish shape that gave it its nickname, with four runways across 2,679 hectares.

Getting in is straightforward if you use the right line. A ground transport centre sits directly beneath the terminal, with the Daxing Airport Express metro and the Beijing to Xiong'an intercity railway both running from it. More rail is built but not yet open. By road it is 46 km south of central Beijing on its own expressway, and it serves the wider Beijing, Tianjin and Hebei region.
after:
Beijing's second international airport, 46 km south of the city centre, opened in September 2019. Its star-shaped terminal of about 700,000 square metres was the world's largest single airport terminal building when it opened.

Beijing Capital, the city's other main airport, is about 65 km to the north. Airlines are split between the two, so check which airport a client's flight uses, particularly for a connection.

There are four runways.
